best_for: Beginners, students and hobby animators who want to draw frame-by-frame 2D animation for free, on modest hardware, without a pro tool's learning curve.

points.title: Plain, light frame-by-frame drawing
points.text: Pencil2D keeps the interface small so you spend your time drawing, not learning menus. It runs on Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD.

points.title: Raster and vector in one project
points.text: You can sketch on raster layers and ink on vector layers, then switch between the two as you go. The canvas is endless; the camera layer sets what ends up in the exported video.

points.title: Free for commercial work
points.text: Pencil2D is open source under GPL 2.0 and free to use, even for paid projects.

points.title: Expect some rough edges
points.text: The team says openly that the app can be buggy and that it relies on volunteers. Turn on autosave in Preferences, and save a new project once before you start, to avoid losing work on long scenes.

points.title: Windows build is a zip
points.text: The Windows listing here offers 32-bit and 64-bit zip files with no installer. Extract all files first; you may need to run the bundled Visual C++ runtime installer if a DLL is missing.

points.title: Mac builds differ by chip
points.text: From 0.7.2 the Mac app is verified by Apple, so the unidentified developer warning is gone. The listing here has a DMG for Apple Silicon and a zip for Intel, which needs macOS 10.14 or later. Legacy builds for older Macs and Windows XP lack security fixes.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is official
points.text: The Flatpak covers x64 and Arm64 and is verified by Flathub as published by the Pencil2D team. Distribution packages also exist for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and Arch.

points.title: Only one version here
points.text: Windows, macOS and Linux each list only the current 0.7.2. Older releases are on the project's GitHub releases page.
